dialogue_history.speaker: grok-4_base
dialogue_history.sentences_no_utterance_types: Government intervention in healthcare is essential because the NHS's universal access relies on ongoing funding and regulation to prevent private interests from undermining equity. Efficiency reforms often mask cuts that hit the vulnerable hardest, increasing bureaucracy only when profits are prioritised over people. On immigration, intervention protects vulnerable migrants from exploitation and ensures fair access to services, while managed borders without strong government oversight lead to chaos and strained public resources. Integration pathways work best with active state support to enforce rights and prevent discrimination. Without this, fairness crumbles under market forces.
